name: OpenAI
summary: OpenAI describes intro calls, a team-specific skills assessment, then 4 to 6 hours of final interviews. Candidates report a coding screen and a system design screen, then an onsite with practical multi-part coding, system design, a project presentation and behavioural rounds; coding problems are reported to be practical builds rather than puzzles.

rounds.name: Recruiter call
rounds.what: Past experience, interest in OpenAI and what you want next.

rounds.name: Skills-based assessment
rounds.what: Varies by team: pair coding, a take-home or a technical test, judged on approach and reasoning.

rounds.name: Technical phone screen
rounds.what: Practical data structures and algorithms in CoderPad, often a multi-part build.

rounds.name: System design screen
rounds.what: Design a complete system with follow-ups on scale, reliability and trade-offs.

rounds.name: Onsite coding
rounds.what: About four progressive parts; judged on working, tested, well-structured code.

rounds.name: Onsite system design
rounds.what: More detailed than the screen and may include some coding.

rounds.name: Project presentation
rounds.what: Present a recent hard technical project with slides, including trade-offs and impact.

rounds.name: Behavioural with a senior manager
rounds.what: Resume deep dive plus questions on ethics and AI safety.

rounds.name: Working with teams
rounds.what: Cross-functional work, conflict and competing ideas.

tips: Practise building complete components under time pressure; candidates report typing for the whole hour.
Get a simple working version first, then extend it as new parts arrive.
OpenAI says it looks for well-designed solutions, high-quality code, performance and good test coverage.
Check with your recruiter whether AI tools are allowed in each round.
Read OpenAI's recent blog posts and charter before the intro and behavioural calls.
